scientific_hypothesis: The remaining zero-candidate case is not caused by query-count limits or exact duplicate response signatures. It may require candidates defined by compositional relations among query outcomes. A deterministic closure system built from label-free implication and equivalence relations over outcome-membership atoms can expose structurally redundant remaining-query sets that neither seeded sampling nor exact-signature grouping can generate.

single_allowed_algorithmic_change.name: response_lattice_closure_generator

response_encoding.unit: For every frozen compiled query q and every outcome token emitted by the frozen compiler for q, create one Boolean atom (q, outcome) whose value on a row is 1 exactly when that row has that emitted outcome for q.
response_encoding.multi_outcome_rule: All compiler-emitted outcomes are represented one-vs-rest; no outcome is selected as privileged and no outcome is discarded.
response_encoding.missing_value_rule: The compiler-emitted missing token is an ordinary explicit outcome atom, treated identically to le, gt, categorical, and other exact outcome tokens.
response_encoding.query_projection_rule: Closure is computed over outcome atoms, but a remaining-query candidate may contain q only when the closed atom set contains the complete atom block for q. Partial outcome blocks are never emitted. Minimal generators are likewise projected to query units only when block-complete.
response_encoding.frozen_source: Outcome tokens and row assignments come only from the unchanged compiled task representation; raw features are not re-read or reinterpreted.

single_allowed_algorithmic_change.description: For each allowed-row set, encode compiler-emitted query outcomes as frozen Boolean membership atoms. Construct a finite closure system using only exact structural relations: atom equivalence, implication, incompatibility, and deterministic intersections of implication-closed generator sets. Emit remaining-query masks only from nontrivial block-complete closed sets and block-complete minimal generators.

canonical_ranking.candidate_key: Serialize the candidate without query indices as: task row count, allowed-row membership vector, sorted multiset of complete query-block signatures, and sorted multiset of generator-block signatures. A query-block signature is the lexicographically sorted tuple of its outcome-atom Boolean vectors over allowed rows. Hash this canonical serialization with SHA-256.
canonical_ranking.deduplication: Candidates with identical canonical serialization are one structural candidate, regardless of query names, query indices, or outcome-token spelling.
canonical_ranking.truncation: Sort unique candidates by the canonical serialization bytes, using SHA-256 only as an integrity digest, and retain the first unchanged maximum-state count. Because neither serialization nor ordering contains query indices, renaming or permuting queries must produce the correspondingly permuted retained set.
canonical_ranking.tie_rule: Canonical-equal candidates are deduplicated before truncation; no index-based tie breaker is permitted.

single_allowed_algorithmic_change.activation: Only when the unchanged v0.84 selector returns zero states.
forbidden_inputs: query indices or outcome-token spelling in candidate ranking
unchanged_components: task compiler and its outcome tokens

implementation_order: implement pure outcome-atom encoding, block projection, response-relation, canonicalization, and closure helpers
test closure axioms on exhaustive small multi-outcome matrices including explicit missing outcomes
test determinism, label independence, query-permutation equivariance, and outcome-token-renaming invariance
test that no partial query outcome block can become an emitted candidate
prove exact preservation of v0.84 state digests on already-contributing tasks
only after a green synthetic gate, add a separate opened-data development workflow
negative_result_policy: Every failed synthetic invariant, coverage gate, correctness gate, or performance threshold is retained permanently. No threshold, encoding, projection, relation definition, canonicalization, or truncation rule may be weakened after inspecting opened-data results.
claim_boundary: This is a preregistered opened-data development hypothesis. Passing it would not constitute untouched external validation, independent reproduction, a world-class result, or a general-AI breakthrough.
